chapter: Arrangements, repertoire and the last band
title: Instructing a police-band saxophonist during Prohibition
summary: At Bernard's during Prohibition a police corporal came nightly for sax instruction and tips and brought a piano copy Laurent turned into a band number.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: No, that wasn't in my number I'll tell you how I got that number There was a Corporal on the police force He was playing alto sax in the police band Well, when I was playing for Bernard Michel out here During the bootlegging time Provision time He used to come on a bandstand every night by me To get a little instruction And They'd bring their music in their pocket And just ask you Say, first knock that out for me And if you play it, you was a good five or ten dollar tip So Every night you'd come sit on a bandstand For two, three hours with me I'd give them a little instruction On his saxophone He said He'd get more out of me The man who was directing the Orgham theater Was his teacher He says he didn't get much As much out of him As he would get out of me for nothing So he'd come every night by me And get instruction And he went on and did good He brought me this number in his pocket He said, play that number It was a piano copy Just a piano copy That's how I had to write it like that So I told him I said, here's flat for you So and so for you We had a five piece band I said, okay, let's go We played the number Well, I played it As written For me Get the sense of it I played it As written So after that I told him I said, now go on out there And dance You're gonna hear the number I'm gonna play it for you now Man, we told that number He gave me the number He gave me the number To each his own The little dream That little dream Got nowhere Show me the way To make love to you Tonight you belong to me Bagdad I used to love to play that
